A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Goldilocks face-verification benchmarks. All pages, tables, figures and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 15 face-recognition models, a domain-control experiment, an identity-overlap ablation and demographic analyses in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised benchmark, identity-overlap and demographic results in Tables 2, 4 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same benchmark-construction procedure, including attribute thresholds, pair selection, age restrictions, image-occurrence limits, demographic balancing and fold construction. Renaming Twins-IND to ND-Twins does not introduce a methodological change.

E1.justification: The proposed benchmarks, source datasets, training datasets and external evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. Both versions describe Hadrian as containing AAM and CM pairs; removing its contradictory female-group rows from Table 5 does not document an actual population change.

E2.justification: The corresponding evaluations retain ArcFace, CurricularFace, MagFace, AdaFace and UniFace. Abbreviated names in v3 Tables 3–5 represent the same methods, and the comparator benchmarks are retained.

E3.justification: Both versions specify ResNet100 models trained on MS1MV2, WebFace4M and Glint360K, the same 6,000-pair benchmark construction and ten-fold accuracy evaluation. The domain-control and overlap experiments retain their stated designs. Revised scores alone do not establish changed settings or reruns.

E4.justification: Two existing analyses are substantially revised. Table 4 replaces consistently higher overlap accuracy with mostly negligible, mixed effects, changing the evidence for identity-disjoint folds. Table 5 removes Hadrian's female-group rows and substantially revises demographic disparities. The domain-control analysis in Table 3 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean ten-fold accuracy without seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The softened language about identity overlap changes interpretation, not statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises average accuracy for Hadrian/Eclipse/twins from 92.33/82.50/71.57 to 92.62/82.81/71.56 under the same stated settings. Table 4 changes ArcFace's Hadrian disjoint-minus-overlap difference from -0.24 to 0. Table 5 reverses Hadrian's demographic ordering: ArcFace AAM/CM accuracy changes from 90.53/91.93 to 97.17/86.27. Eclipse disparities become roughly 30 percentage points. These are substantive result revisions, not established methodological gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The construction constraints and evaluation definitions remain unchanged; the new discussion of exploiting attribute patterns is informal reasoning.

C1.justification: The three-benchmark contribution and main difficulty claims remain. v3 narrows the twins novelty claim from an absence of identical-twins test sets to an absence of such sets using the LFW protocol. The abstract also qualifies its difficulty comparison as against test sets with added artifacts.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the claim that identity overlap significantly increases accuracy with an acknowledgment of slight changes, justifying disjointness through design rigor instead. It also adds an argument that exploiting fixed attribute patterns would harm performance elsewhere and require difficult data collection. These substantially revise the discussion supporting the benchmark design.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset-specific access link, explicitly states noncommercial use and explains the ND-Twins license requirement arising from original IRB conditions. It removes the anonymous training-platform URL. These change access documentation without establishing changed implementation or resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Vijayan et al.'s Twins 3D Face Recognition Challenge and acknowledges existing twins benchmarks while distinguishing its LFW-format contribution. Phillips et al.'s twins study was already cited in v2; its duplicated v3 reference is not another distinct added work.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain intact. Changes include the Twins-IND/ND-Twins renaming, numeric citation style, localized wording refinements, a rewritten overlap interpretation and added paragraphs on attribute-pattern exploitation and access.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from one-column to two-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. New Figure 1 visualizes existing Table 2 comparisons. The original example figures are retained and renumbered; Table 5 loses two rows, and Tables 3–5 abbreviate method headings.

improvement.justification: v3 improves internal consistency by aligning Hadrian's demographic rows with its male-only construction, moderating the overlap interpretation to match Table 4, and narrowing the twins novelty claim. Access terms are clearer. These are limited gains: substantial score revisions remain unexplained, and Table 5's caption and discussion give inconsistent demographic-gap figures, 30.26% and 30.62%.
